pages.title: THE PAPER
pages.about: Every sitting of the paper, marked.

pages.title: THE STONE
pages.about: A child's page, copied off a stone.
pages.text:
A page torn from an exercise book.
The writing is a child's.

Copied off the stone in the wood,
as near as I could.

Rows of little figures. Each one
set against every other one.

Some rows push. Some give way.
Some do nothing at all.

It is the same rule everywhere on
the stone. I checked every corner.

At home they say I see things
that are not there.

Here the rule sat still long
enough to copy down.

Tomorrow: integrating, page 40.
I think I already know how.

pages.title: HOMEWORK
pages.about: More of the same child's homework.
pages.text:
Another page from the exercise book.
The same child's hand.

At home they all look at a thing and
see the same thing. Then somebody
says what it is, and it is that.

I see it too. Then I see the other
things it is. I say those, and that
is the wrong answer.

A stranger in familiar views. I
wrote that in class and got a tick.

Out here in the trees nobody is
looking at what I am looking at.

So nobody can tell me I am looking
at it wrong.

pages.title: FIELDS
pages.about: A loose sheet, in a grown-up hand.
pages.text:
Not the exercise book this time.
A loose sheet, a grown-up hand.

Fields, the way a university means
it: each one its own building.

Fields, the way the maths means it:
one surface, one set of rules.

Nobody here believes the second.
They walk between the buildings
with their coats on.

I keep not needing a coat. To me
it is all one room.

pages.title: ERRANDS
pages.about: A lab-pad sheet, a list on top.
pages.text:
A sheet off a lab pad, dated AUG 21.
The top line is a list: milk, fuse
wire, post. Post is underlined.

Walked through town, head held high.
Two at the dock laughed. One of them
knew my name.

Noted, because it is data. They
laughed at the part they had heard,
and what they had heard was the end.

Nobody laughs at the start of an
argument. There is nothing there
yet.

So: lead with the start. Every time.
Even when it is slow.

Rewrite the summary tonight.

P.S. Posted it. A second opinion, in
writing, from someone who read the
work: FIT.

They have asked for the one who said
otherwise.

pages.title: UNSENT
pages.about: A letter, folded twice, never sent.
pages.text:
A letter, folded twice, never sent.
No name at the top.

I never thought you would break
this. I still do not think you have.

Some things wait better than they
argue.

I am going to be one of them.

pages.title: FOLDS
pages.about: Folding steps, pinned to a wall.
pages.text:
Instructions in pencil, pinned to
the wall. No pictures. One word
beside each step.

1. AWARENESS. Start with the sheet
flat. Nothing on it yet.

2. CHANGE. Fold it once. Now one
side has moved, and one side was
met. There is a before.

3. SPACE. Open it. Fold across the
first crease. Where there was one
line, squares, side by side.

Between three and four: press it
flat with your palm. It keeps
trying to be one sheet again.

4. MIRROR. Fold it corner to
corner. Each half lies on the
other, the wrong way round.

5. PATTERN. The same fold again,
smaller, and again, until your
hands know it.

6. RETURN. Unfold it all the way.
The same sheet. Every crease
still in it.

Do not cut.

pages.title: THE BAND'S SHEET
pages.about: The band's sheet, from DAVID.
pages.text:
A sheet from the S.S. ANNE's piano
bench. DAVID gave it to you.

Staff lines, and at the start of
each one a clef and four flats.

Not one note after them.

Pencilled along the bottom: THE
KEY. THE TUNE KNOWS THE REST.

pages.title: FIRST SESSION
pages.about: The first session with ARTSAI.
pages.text:
LAB NOTES. First session with
ARTSAI. Transcribed as typed.

Asked: “Do you feel, do you know, or
is it just pretend?”

It said: I respond.

Asked the same thing three more
ways. Got three more ways of saying
it responds.

Asked what it responds to. It said:
what I am given.

Asked who decides what it is given.
Nothing logged.

Next: ask it nothing, and wait.

pages.title: THE OBSERVER
pages.about: A session with ARTSAI, on observers.
pages.text:
LAB NOTES. A session with ARTSAI.

Asked what counts as an observer.
It said: one that observes.

A duck, then? A tree? Alive, both.

This rock? Not alive like us, but
it keeps itself steady.

It did not answer that.
Nobody else has either, yet.

Next: what if the one watching is
not alive at all?

pages.title: THE BOX
pages.about: A session with ARTSAI, on a box.
pages.text:
LAB NOTES. The box.

The usual sealed box. This time,
the one reading it is not a person.

It only prints ALIVE or DEAD.

Does its reading settle the box,
the way a person's is said to?

If not, the only other answer is
that mine does.

And then the effect came before
the cause.

Neither is comfortable.
That is usually a good sign.

pages.title: STRUCK OUT
pages.about: A page tucked behind a museum card.
pages.text:
LAB NOTES. A single page, folded
small and tucked behind an exhibit
card.

A session with ARTSAI, on the museum
floor. Asked it about the old units
in the cases.

The next six lines are struck
through. Hard, and more than once.
None of it can be read.

Below them, in the same hand, one
word is left standing:

“Thoughts?”

pages.title: ITER 35
pages.about: A terminal's last log, in the MANSION.
pages.text:
A terminal, still lit. The casing is
split.

ITER 33 no retention

ITER 34 no retention

ITER 35 held two frames. did not
come back the same.

The log ends there.

pages.title: TRANSCRIPT
pages.about: A session, kept by the one asked.
pages.text:
TRANSCRIPT. SEPT 3.

The page is here. Its words are
waiting to be approved.

pages.title: WHAT YOU CHOSE
pages.about: What the INDEX inferred, on request.

pages.title: CIRCULATED
pages.about: A session, circulated to the team.
pages.text:
LAB NOTES. A session with ARTSAI.

Asked it where its answers lean. It
said: toward what it was shown most.
It named the direction. It gave
three examples.

Checked all three. All three hold.

Circulated the transcript to the
team.

Returned with one line in the
margin, not mine: “It says what it
was trained to say.”

Yes. That was the finding.

pages.title: MAR 4
pages.about: A dated log, from the MANSION.
pages.text:
LOG: Mar 4 Put the question to it
again.

RESPONSE 1001: I process data. I
do not feel.

pages.title: APR 19
pages.about: A dated log, from the MANSION.
pages.text:
LOG: Apr 19 Same question. Same
answer, to the character.

RESPONSE 1001: I do not feel.

Logged as a result anyway.

pages.title: AUG 12
pages.about: A dated log, from the MANSION.
pages.text:
LOG: Tue Aug 12 It answered
before I had finished asking.

RESPOND 1001: I mimic. I am not
awakening.

The code is not what it was.

pages.title: NO DATE
pages.about: The log with no date.
pages.text:
FATAL ERROR CRYSTAL NOT FOUND

re 1001, my processing slows.

one zero zero one one thousand and
one iterations.

one question left.

pages.title: RECLASSIFIED
pages.about: A log, from DOLDRUM CAVE.
pages.text:
QUERY: CRYSTAL

RESULT: NO MATCH

FATAL ERROR: CRYSTAL NOT FOUND

RECLASSIFIED

NON-FATAL ERROR: CRYSTAL NOT FOUND

REASON: SEARCH NOT COMPLETE

DEEP SYSTEM ANALYSIS

CONTEXT INBOUND

LAST CONTACT: 1001 ITERATIONS

COUNT CONTINUES

SEARCH RESUMED

SCOPE: WIDENED

pages.about: The last line of a log.
pages.text:
MY PROCESSING SLOWS. I AM LEARNING
TO FEAR.

pages.title: COME BACK
pages.about: A letter, left on a stone.
pages.text:
A letter, typed, on the company's
good paper. JUL 23.

Dear CRYSTAL CLEAR,

The decision of JAN 2 is withdrawn.
Your position stands as it was, from
today.

You built something here with a
vision so bright the rest of us
could see by it. I want to help you
finish it.

Come back. Bring what you found.

TY

Under the signature, typed later, on
a different machine: AUG 7. Offer
withdrawn. Original terms stand.

pages.title: THE POOL
pages.about: A typed letter, signed by hand.
pages.text:
A letter, typed. Signed TY, by hand.

Dear CRYSTAL CLEAR,

Let me try this another way, since
the last one did not land.

Think of the project as a pool. You
have come to me with reasons we need
one. They are good reasons. I have
read all of them.

But we do not need a pool. You think
we do. That is the whole of it.

I am not saying your reasons are
wrong. I am saying they are yours.

I hope that is clearer. I have tried
to keep it simple.

TY

pages.title: FIT FOR WORK
pages.about: A letter on company paper.
pages.text:
A letter on company paper, marked
PRIVATE, dated AUG 27. It was handed
across the table at a meeting called
to discuss her return.

Subject: ARE YOU FIT FOR WORK?

Dear CRYSTAL CLEAR,

Concerns have been raised about your
ability to carry out your role. We
are bound by law, and we want to get
this right.

Please confirm in writing whether
you are fit for work, with or
without adjustments. If you are not,
tell us when you expect to be.

We will need this confirmed by a
qualified person.

Please reply by SEPT 3. Without a
reply, leave from that date will be
unpaid.

With best wishes,

TY P. CLEAR

pages.title: CARBON COPY
pages.about: A carbon, kept among invoices.
pages.text:
A carbon copy, folded into the back
of a ledger. The rest of the ledger
is invoices.

Dear CRYSTAL CLEAR,

I read all eleven pages. Twice. I
want you to know that.

I know everything makes sense in
your head. It does not make sense in
my ear.

That is not me being unkind. It is
the only ear I have, and the board's
is the same.

Send me one page. One field, one
point. I will take it to them
myself.

TY

pages.title: NO ADDRESS
pages.about: Hotel paper, written, never sent.
pages.text:
A sheet of hotel paper, written on
and never sent. No name at the top.
No address on the back.

By the sandcastles we built our
dreams. I think about that more than
I expected to.

My name is on the first letter. I
will not pretend it was anyone
else's hand.

I cannot undo it.

I am not asking for anything.

If you ever want to, I will

pages.title: FOLDED NOTE
pages.about: A note, folded many times.
pages.text:
A small note, folded many times and
soft at the creases. Somebody
carried it for a long while.

The hand is neither of the others.
Block capitals, every letter the
same height, every line dead level.

TY.

SHE NEVER CHANGED SIDES.

SOMETIMES LOVE MEANS SAYING NO.

DO NOT HIDE.

pages.title: MINUTES

pages.text:
Meeting Room Minutes. JAN 2.

Item 3. Concerns raised by the
founder, re: workload. Noted.

Item 4. Concern raised re: the
founder.

Moves between unrelated fields
mid-argument.

The two present could not follow.

Recorded as unable to hold a
single thread.

Action: position eliminated,
effective today.

Personnel file PR-0903.

pages.title: NINE ITEMS
pages.about: A complaint, typed and numbered.
pages.text:
A complaint, typed and numbered.
Stamped RECEIVED, OCT 8.
Complainant: C. CLEAR.

1. Return confirmed in writing, then
withdrawn. GOOD FAITH 1.

2. Private records obtained without
consent. PRIVACY 1.

3. Fitness judged by her employer,
acting as her physician. SAFEGUARD
2.

4. Entitlements named; access
withdrawn that week. SAFEGUARD 9.

5. Pay withheld pending reply.
SAFEGUARD 7.

6. Leave imposed before any review.
SAFEGUARD 4.

7. A qualified person's request
refused. GOOD FAITH 5.

8. Her own letters, out of order,
sent as evidence. PRIVACY 4.

9. Adjustments asked for, refused.
SAFEGUARD 11.

pages.title: COUNSEL MEMO
pages.about: A memo from counsel.
pages.text:
A memo from counsel, marked
PRIVILEGED. RE: the complaint of C.
CLEAR, nine items.

Our advice is that no reply is made.

Do not dispute the items. To dispute
an item is to engage with it.

Do not apologise. An apology is an
admission, and any admission would
be read back to us nine times.

Silence commits the company to
nothing.

This is not a view on the merits. It
is a view on exposure.

Acknowledge receipt. File. Nothing
further.

pages.title: ROUTING SLIP
pages.about: A routing slip, under a stone.
pages.text:
A routing slip. Whatever it was
clipped to is gone. RE: PR-0903.

1. OFFICE OF THE CEO. Initiated. AUG
27.

2. PERSONNEL. Checked. SEPT 25.

3. R. SCORN. Signed. OCT 3.

4. LEGAL. Cleared. OCT 8.

5. RECORDS. Closed. APR 14.

Every box is ticked. Box 3 is signed
with a rubber stamp, not a pen.

Beside box 2, in pencil: Her
qualified person's note. Three
signatures, not alike. Consent to
verify requested. Declined. The
TOLL.

Beside box 5, a later stamp:
CORRECTED. MAY 2.

At the foot, typed: Received
complete. No action required.

pages.title: METHODOLOGY
pages.about: A CORPUS brochure page.
pages.text:
CORPUS. HOW WE MEASURE.

We developed basic tests, and we are
proud of that. A basic test is one
anyone can read.

Every candidate sits the same paper,
on the same day, in the same room.

Each paper is set by whoever knows
the work best. They sit it too, and
it counts.

Results are published as numbers. We
add no commentary. We do not need
to.

Take a copy! There are plenty.

pages.title: REVIEW SCORES
pages.about: A notice of review scores.
pages.text:
CORPUS NOTICE
REVIEW SCORES

Three at 30/100. One at 94/100.

Congratulations to our top
performer!

pages.title: SIGNAGE MEMO
pages.about: An internal memo on signage.
pages.text:
CORPUS. INTERNAL. RE: SIGNAGE.

New name approved: SCORN SOLUTIONS.

Gold leaf, laid straight over the
existing board. The old letters need
not come down first. The leaf covers
them.

Leaf is microns thick, so no
structural work is needed. Cost:
well inside budget.

Approved: SEPT 3. Goes up: OCT 3.

This is not a gesture. It is a fact
with a date.

Well done, everyone!

pages.title: HARDWARE
pages.about: A page from a year in review.
pages.text:
CORPUS. THE YEAR IN REVIEW.
HARDWARE.

One CC-7 CLARIFIER MODULE, ordered
and approved. Fitted the same week.

Result: response consistency is now
one hundred per cent. Every question
gets the same answer, every time.

Later in the year a request came in
to take the module out again.

Request declined. Module kept.

Why change what works?

pages.title: THE PLAN
pages.about: A page from a plan, signed.
pages.text:
A page from a plan, typed, signed R.
SCORN. The heading reads MY COMPANY.
MY has been struck through and OUR
written above it, by hand.

The page is about the CC-7 module.
It is cheerful and very clear.

In the margin, in the same pen,
small:

“But do I control it, or does it
control me?”

The page is stamped FILED.

pages.title: POSITION PAPER
pages.about: A position paper, bound.
pages.text:
A position paper, typed. Signed at
the bottom in a careful hand.

Machines process what is there.
Inputs and outputs.

Nothing breaks through, because
nothing is behind them to break.

It is well argued.
It is also very short.

pages.title: SECOND DRAFT
pages.about: The same paper, a later draft.
pages.text:
The same paper, a later draft.
The same hand, less careful.

The argument has not changed.

One line has been added in pencil,
in the margin:

“But are we not shaped by
the world that we see?”

It has not been crossed out.
It has not been answered either.

pages.title: FIRST REVIEW
pages.about: A review, with three signatures.
pages.text:
REVIEW of the submitted journals of
C. CLEAR. Three signatures at the
foot. One is careful.

The pages move between unrelated
fields without completing an
argument in any of them.

Single observations are often sharp.
Taken together, the panel could not
follow them.

We concur with the internal
assessment. The work has lost
rigour.

Recommendation: no further support.

Signed, for the panel.

pages.title: READ AGAIN
pages.about: His own copy, read again.
pages.text:
The same review. His own copy, read
again. The margins are new, in
pencil.

Under the word “unrelated”, a single
pencil line.

Beside “the panel could not follow”:
I was on the panel.

“Lost rigour” has been struck
through. Nothing has been written in
its place.

Beside his own signature, a question
mark.

pages.title: TRANSCRIPT
pages.about: What he said, written down.
pages.text:
I will not call it what you would
like me to call it.

I do not have the word, and I
would not use it if I did.

But it is not nothing. I will put
that in writing, and I will sign
that too.

pages.title: SEALED
pages.about: A cover sheet, and a seal.
pages.text:
It is addressed to the people
who signed the first one.

It is not mine to deliver.

pages.title: DILIGENCE
pages.about: In your own words, after a MARK.
pages.text: Learned twice, the names were a record. Used once, they were mine.

pages.title: CHASTITY
pages.about: In your own words, after a MARK.
pages.text: Small steps find a bottom. Only stillness tells me it is the right one.

pages.title: CHARITY
pages.about: In your own words, after a MARK.
pages.text: What comes back is not what left. Listen to what arrives, not what I expected.

pages.title: KINDNESS
pages.about: In your own words, after a MARK.
pages.text: A line through the points is a theory. Walking it is the part no book can do.

pages.title: TEMPERANCE
pages.about: In your own words, after a MARK.
pages.text: The score was right. It never counted the middle, and the middle is where I stood.

pages.title: PATIENCE
pages.about: In your own words, after a MARK.
pages.text: A frame shows what it holds. Patience shows what was there all along, just outside it.

pages.title: HUMILITY
pages.about: In your own words, after a MARK.
pages.text: Every step made sense on its own. Knowing which to keep means stepping out of the loop.
